solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Frost deposit — degrees start falling

indicators.note: falling says a letter drops out of the stash word

parts.note: a deposit, a stored-up stash, is a hoard

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of degrees

explanation.surface: A weather report: frost settling as the temperature begins to drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost deposit' looks like one phrase for the definition, but 'deposit' is HOARD; D (start of 'degrees') falls out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoar is white frost, the icy coating of crystals on grass and branches.

clue.text: Blockbuster rehung 'mid confusion

indicators.note: in confusion means the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: 'mid is a poetic short form of amid, read as its letters

explanation.surface: Something rehung amid chaos, like a picture put back during a messy move.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an outstanding, sensational thing, as is a blockbuster.

clue.text: Salts, a large order from David's son

parts.note: old salts are sailors; ABs are able seamen
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Bath salts and a big order placed by one of David's sons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salts' tempts as anagram fodder, but it means sailors (ABS, able seamen). The OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Absalom is the third son of King David, who rebelled against him.

clue.text: Great anger finding vermin in outskirts of Wisbech

indicators.note: in places the vermin inside the letters taken from the town name
outskirts are the edges, so the town's first and last letters

parts.note: a rat is a classic example of vermin

explanation.surface: Fury at discovering rats on the edge of a Cambridgeshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Wisbech is a market town in Cambridgeshire; its outskirts are W and H, around RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is intense anger, often righteous or vengeful.

clue.text: Ebb-tide

parts.note: read literally, an ebb is a falling and a tide is a body of moving water

explanation.surface: The sea going out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the sea receding; split the answer into two words to see the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade of river water dropping over a cliff is, punningly, the ebb or fall of water.

clue.text: Expose piece of hair causing stoppage of flow in pipe

parts.note: to air something is to expose it to view or to the open
a lock is a tress or curl of hair

explanation.surface: A stray bit of hair exposed and clogging the plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlock is a bubble trapped in a pipe that blocks the flow of liquid.

clue.text: He had the measure of the old king

parts.note: a rod is an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.surface: A man who sized up an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A rod (or pole) is an old British measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod the Great was king of Judaea at the time of Jesus' birth in the Gospels.

clue.text: Account held in part agreement

indicators.note: held in means one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: An account kept as part of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Lady has name of aristocrat

parts.note: Patricia is a woman's name, standing for any lady

explanation.surface: A woman bears the name of a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrician was a member of Rome's noble class, hence any aristocrat.

clue.text: Study manufacture of lace or hide

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: manufacture of means the letters are worked into a new product

explanation.surface: Learning about lacemaking or about leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a noun (animal skin) beside lace, but it is the verb. CEAL is the anagram of LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight.

clue.text: Explaining wrongly cover during exceptional springtime

indicators.note: during places the cover word in the middle of the rearranged season
exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to cover with earth

explanation.surface: Getting it wrong about burial during an unusual spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' reads as a noun but is the verb to bury; 'exceptional' rearranges the season into MISPRETING, which 'during' opens up for the burial word.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinterpret is to take or explain the meaning wrongly.

clue.text: I name dishonest person said to be at outcrop

indicators.note: said to be signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: a liar is a dishonest person

explanation.surface: Someone admits being the dishonest one at the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology an inlier is an outcrop of older rock surrounded by younger strata.

clue.text: Experienced hand getting on with little Timothy expressing hesitation

parts.note: getting on means growing old
Tim is the short form of Timothy
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A veteran with young Tim, who hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is a veteran with long experience of a job or place.

clue.text: James reportedly, before break, had cheap gadget

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like the short form of the name

parts.note: Jim is a short form of James
a crack is a break or fracture

explanation.surface: James, they say, had a cheap gadget before it broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimcrack is a showy but flimsy, worthless trinket.

clue.text: Sharp practice seen in series of tight turns on track

parts.note: a chicane is a sequence of tight bends on a racing circuit
RY, railway, is a track

explanation.surface: Dirty tricks on the tight bends of a race circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery or deception, especially underhand dealing.

clue.text: Choke regulates itself

indicators.note: regulates means adjusts or puts in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engine's choke controls itself automatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choke' reads as the car part, but it is the verb meaning smother.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to suffocate or choke, or to suppress.

clue.text: Demanding headmistress fully content

indicators.note: content means what something contains, so the answer is inside these words

explanation.surface: A demanding headmistress who is fully satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'satisfied', but it means what is contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressful task is demanding, putting one under strain.

clue.text: Startling enlightenment as a result of raising the lid

definitions.meaning: a revelation that surprises and informs
something that lifts the eyelid open, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: the lid is an eyelid, and the answer opens it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation; literally it is what opens an eye.

clue.text: Right to have a face on this tyre?

parts.note: a dial is a clock face; dial is also slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tyre ought to have a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial is a tyre whose cords run radially across the tread.

clue.text: Runner's two 18s allowed to be included

parts.note: 18-down is ARTICLE, and a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to be included puts the allowed word inside the second article

parts.note: the is the definite article, the second of the pair
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A runner allowed two items included.
explanation.walkthrough: '18s' points to the answer of 18-down: two kinds of article, the indefinite and the definite, with 'to be included' setting the permission word inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a sportsperson, such as a track runner.

clue.text: Unperturbed about commercial song

indicators.note: about means around, so the calm word goes round the advert

parts.note: serene means calm and unperturbed
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: Calm about singing a jingle for an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song sung to a loved one, often beneath a window.

clue.text: Did not stand heartless antic that was wicked

parts.note: someone who sat did not stand

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A wicked prank by someone who stayed seated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes T, the centre of ANTIC, leaving ANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, as wicked as Satan.

clue.text: An editorial? Either

definitions.meaning: an is the indefinite ... in grammar
an editorial is a newspaper piece

explanation.walkthrough: 'Either' says both words define the answer: 'an' is a grammatical article and an editorial is a newspaper one.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is both a word like a or the and a piece of writing in a newspaper.

clue.text: Hick cuddling hot bird

indicators.note: cuddling means holding close, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a hick or country bumpkin is a peasant
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin hugging a hot bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheasant is a long-tailed game bird.

clue.text: Of the ear or of the mouth, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word sounding like another when spoken

parts.note: oral means of the mouth

explanation.surface: Is it the ear or the mouth? We hear it's one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural means relating to the ear or to hearing.

clue.text: Made fun of nurse put out

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade

indicators.note: out means displaced or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse is mocked and annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like a phrase meaning annoyed, but 'out' scrambles PUT into TUP. SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone up is British slang for to parody or mock them.

clue.text: New place in green for bird

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: Finding a new place on the green for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a fast bird of prey.

clue.text: Quails be on both sides of valley

definitions.note: the definition is plural birds; the answer is the collective noun for a group of them

indicators.note: both sides of takes the first and last letters of valley

explanation.surface: Quail birds perched on either side of a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quails' looks like a verb (cowers), but it is the birds; a bevy is a flock of quails.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevy is the collective noun for a flock of quails.

clue.text: Buffalo calf penned nearby

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the answer is kept inside these words

explanation.surface: A buffalo calf kept in a pen close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Local means near at hand, in the neighbourhood.

clue.text: Overpriced honey?

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.definitionFit: Dear means both expensive and beloved, as in a fond form of address.
